correctness.rationale: Every acyclic orientation of a two-clique coalescence corresponds bijectively to independent uniform permutations, one for each clique. Their centered-rank covariances give C=(a+1)t²L(K_a)/12+(b+1)s²L(K_b)/12. Contrast eigenspaces and the remaining three-dimensional quotient yield eigenvalues 0, au, bv and the two roots of λ²-(au+bv)λ+nuv; the quadratic is negative at au and bv, proving that its smaller/larger roots are globally extremal even for clique size two. The exact identity κ+2+κ^(-1)=4ab/n+(ay-b)²/(ny), y=u/v>0, gives a unique positive minimizer and explicit gap, while roots and product give the sharp imbalanced limit. The packaged standalone program separately enumerates zonotope vertices and checks 217 covariance entries in 6 profiles, plus 1014 exact ratio tests; these finite checks are not asserted to prove the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Compared the weighted covariance and global conditioning optimization with exact unweighted coalescence spectra, zonotope deformation theory, acyclic reorientation theory, relevant graph-spectral variants and recoverable earlier findings. The unweighted spectrum and the equal-weight/equal-size subcase are covered by previous work and expressly excluded from originality. The searched, materially inspected primary results do not provide the unrestricted positive two-clique scale-ratio optimization or its bounded-vs-quadratic asymptotic; historical-priority risk from an unlocated equivalent weighted Laplacian formulation remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent two-coefficient clique-coalescence Laplacian spectral conditioning result might appear in network optimization or preconditioning sources under other terminology; full historical priority has not been independently certified.

The result is not a theorem about vertex-uniform covariance on arbitrary block graphs and does not cover volume-uniform or independent-edge-sign sampling.

value.rationale: A naturally defined geometric anisotropy objective for uniformly sampled graphical-zonotope vertices is optimized over the nontrivial continuous relative edge-weight parameter. For every two-clique size pair the optimal ratio is unique and explicit, the full covariance eigenspectrum and degeneracies are classified, and tuning converts quadratic anisotropy growth in the highly imbalanced unweighted family into an exact bounded limit. These are meaningful infinite-family weighted-design and geometric-conditioning features; not merely a single numerical example or a cosmetic normalization.
